method: four-arm olfactometer, 18 x 18 cm arena, two diagonally opposite arms with 10 uL odorant on filter paper and two with n-hexane control, 100 mL/min airflow per arm, arena rotated 90 degrees between trials, 5 min per wasp; a continuous stay of 10 s or more was defined as a valid olfactory choice (5th percentile of the total sample); chi-square test
conditions: mated females under 12 h old, reared on Corcyra cephalonica eggs and fed 10% sucrose; 30 wasps per concentration per odorant (20 odorants, concentrations 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10 ug/uL); 25 C, 70% RH; the text gives no p values for citral or linalool (they are in Figure 2S and 2N) and does not report the other concentrations of these two compounds, so the quoted concentrations are those the text names as attractive, not a threshold; the paper's own subsampling check gave 5th-percentile thresholds of 8, 10 and 12 s for samples of 30, 50 and 80, and three other odorants had no effect once the threshold was set to 10 s; the same Results section reports the Chilo suppressalis sex pheromone attractive at 1 ug/uL, Z11-16:Ald attractive and Z9-16:Ald repellent at 10 ug/uL
